Bermuda: Companies Act 1981; Proceeds of Crime Act 1997; Anti-Money Laundering Regulations 2008 (as amended); Beneficial Ownership Transparency Act 2020.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all prospective directors, shareholders, UBOs and authorized signatories against the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, EU Financial Sanctions List and Gibraltar Sanctions Regulations 2020. PEP classification applies to foreign, domestic and international-organisation PEPs as well as family members and close associates, triggering enhanced due diligence. Jurisdictions blacklisted by FATF are automatically high-risk, requiring enhanced scrutiny. Continuous monitoring is required post-incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All proposed company names must be submitted in English using the Latin alphabet. A non-Latin script equivalent requires submission of a verified Roman-alphabet transliteration. Names must include a statutory corporate suffix ('Limited', 'Ltd', 'Public Limited Company' or 'PLC') and must not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing or reserved name in the Gibraltar Companies Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant may, within 14 working days of the notice, file Form NR-APPEAL with the Gibraltar Companies Registry, attaching the original rejection notice and a written statement of grounds. The Registrar must rule on the appeal within 21 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may file an application for judicial review or statutory appeal in the Supreme Court of Gibraltar within 28 days of the denial notice, subject to the court fees and procedural rules in the Gibraltar Court Fees Order.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable for a licensed IP patent prosecution agency in Gibraltar. The GFSC requires a physical, accessible registered office with staffing during business hours, although a registered office service provider may be used for filing purposes before licensing; full commercial substance is assessed at the licensing stage.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Gibraltar Companies Act 2014 (Cap. 174, as amended), ss. 1-10 (registration and incorporation), ss. 15-22 (memorandum and articles), ss. 45-68 (directors and secretary), s. 101 (registered office), Part XII (share capital and allotment); read with the Income Tax Act 2010, Pt IV, territorial tax rules conferring zero-tax on non-Gibraltar-source profits and replicating the Bermuda Exempted Company (ELF_CUSTOM_BM_EX) tax-exempt profile.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies House Gibraltar, Registry Services Directorate, Gibraltar Financial Services Commission (GFSC).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form G-001 (Application for Registration of a Company), executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, statutory declaration of compliance (Form G-009), and Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum issued or paid-up capital. Shares may be issued at par or at a premium and may be partly paid; no escrow deposit is required. The first allotment must be recorded in the register of members and notified by allotment return (Form G-006).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the share subscriptions be accepted and the issued shares allotted to the founding subscriber(s) as recorded in the register; (2) that the registered office at [address in Gibraltar] be and is hereby adopted as the Company's statutory registered office under section 101 of the Companies Act 2014, and the officers instruct the registered agent accordingly; (3) that [Name] be and is appointed sole director/chairman, [Name] secretary, and [Name] resident agent for the purposes of the Gibraltar regime; (4) that the director be authorized to open bank accounts, execute the business licence application, and engage counsel to finalize licensing and patent prosecution formalities; and (5) that certified copies of this resolution be filed as corporate governance records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Pre-Clearance and Suitability Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar Companies House — Name Reservation Desk (online via the GFSC e-Companies portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a company-name reservation request for the intended Latin-character corporate name; verify that the name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, does not imply a regulated activity, and is not offensive; receive a written name-clearance notification before executing incorporation documents.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form
Proposed corporate name and variant list
Identification of subscriber(s) and ultimate beneficial owner(s)
Covering letter from the formation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, the agent resubmits an alternate name or files a written representation with the Registrar under s. 6(3) of the Companies Act 2014; a produced clearance is usually granted within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Gibraltar notary public and founding subscribers; registered agent of the formation firm
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the memorandum and articles using the ELF_CUSTOM_BM_EX exempted-company template; each subscriber executes the memorandum in the presence of a notary (or delivers an apostilled power of attorney for corporate subscribers); annex the share subscription schedule and the directors' consents; notarize all signatures before submission.
required_dossiers: Executed Memorandum of Association
Executed Articles of Association
Share subscription schedule
Directors' and secretary's consents (Form G-008)
Notarized evidence of identity and registered address of each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If execution is queried, re-execute before the notary and file a corrective statutory declaration; a fresh certification page is accepted without restarting the incorporation filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment of State Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies House Gibraltar — Registry Filing Window / e-Companies electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge Form G-001 together with the notarized memorandum and articles, the s. 9 compliance declaration, the registered office consent, and the prescribed fee; retain the registry receipt and the stamped duplicate; the Registrar then issues the Certificate of Incorporation with the company number and incorporation date.
required_dossiers: Form G-001 (signed by agent or subscriber)
Memorandum and Articles of Association (paper and PDF)
Statutory declaration of compliance (Form G-009)
Registered office consent form (Form G-004)
State fee payment confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a defective filing, the registry issues a 'notice of rejection' describing the defect; the agent has fourteen days to file the cure document; an unreasonable refusal may be appealed to the Supreme Court of Gibraltar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office, Statutory Registers and Share Certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed corporate service provider / resident agent in Gibraltar; address verified with Companies House
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm the physical Gibraltar registered office (no P.O. box) and file the address notification; open the statutory registers (members, directors, secretary, charges, ultimate beneficial owners); minute the first board resolution; issue share certificates signed by the directors; submit the allotment return for the first share issuance.
required_dossiers: Registered office address notification (Form G-004)
Directors' and secretary's consents and registered particulars
Register of members and first allotment schedule
Signed share certificates
Minute book and corporate seal (if adopted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the address is rejected, provide a lease or title certificate for the premises and resubmit the notification; the register is deemed corrected from the original notification date once accepted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Officer Activation, and Continuing Compliance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company secretary / registered agent, with filings to Companies House Gibraltar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting (or adopt a written resolution under s. 77 of the Companies Act 2014) to confirm the chairman, secretary and resident agent, open the corporate bank account, approve the business licence application, and set the financial year-end; file the first confirmation statement and, where relevant, the annual return; retain the AML/KYC file consistent with the Proceeds of Crime Act 2015 and the GFSC guidance applicable to a low-risk IP agency.
required_dossiers: First board resolution (minutes or written resolution)
Officer appointment records
Allotment return (Form G-006) for first share issue
Confirmation statement / annual return (Form G-005)
AML/KYC file of the non-resident beneficial owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a filing is late, the agent submits a late-filing explanation and, if the Registrar imposes a penalty, a mitigation request supported by a director's certificate; consistent cures have historically reduced or waived penalties for first defaults.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Business Licensing Office, Enterprise Department, HM Government of Gibraltar (with integrated verification by the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission where the agency offers IP-holding or trust-like services)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Gibraltar Business Licence — Category: Professional and Other Business Services (IP and Patent Prosecution Agency), issued under the Gibraltar Business Licensing regime and renewable annually.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of the Environment, Sustainability and Climate Change (DESCC), HM Government of Gibraltar
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration tier — Schedule 2 low-impact activity (office-based professional services); Full EIA Report not required; a simple environmental registration is filed once pre-operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Only sanitary wastewater to the public sewer; zero industrial effluent; VOC concentrations below 0.5 g/m³ for any cleaning/printing consumables; segregated confidential paper and WEEE disposal under the Waste Management Ordinance; standby generator compliance with the ambient air quality limits retained in the Environment Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety compliance certificate from the Gibraltar Fire & Rescue Service (alarm, emergency lighting and evacuation route certification); structural load and building safety inspection certificate for the registered office; Health and Safety at Work Act (Gibraltar) workplace clearance including first-aid, welfare and fire-drill records.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Gibraltar: HM Government of Gibraltar, Income Tax Office (Commissioner of Income Tax), Durbar House, 179 Queen's Road, Gibraltar; primary online portal is the 'One Gibraltar' digital services platform (portal.gibraltar.gov.gi) and e-filing via the Income Tax Office self-assessment system. Bermuda (incorporation state): Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, and the Office of the Tax Commissioner for payroll tax purposes; no income tax return is required for a Bermuda Exempted Company.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Register the Bermuda Exempted Company as an External Company (overseas company) with the Gibraltar Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act 2014, filing certified charter documents, a list of directors, and a Gibraltar registered office address for service of process. Step 2 — Apply to the Gibraltar Income Tax Office for a Gibraltar Tax Reference Number (TRN) using the corporate registration form, attaching (a) the Bermuda Certificate of Incorporation, (b) the Gibraltar External Company registration certificate, (c) particulars of directors and shareholders, and (d) a declaration of the place of central management and control; processing takes approximately 7–14 working days. Step 3 — Register the entity with the relevant Gibraltar professional licensing body for patent and trademark agency work (patent attorney/trademark agent licensing is a statutory prerequisite for the ISIC_7490_02 scope) and, if staff are engaged in Gibraltar, register as an employer for income tax (PAYE) and social insurance. Step 4 — File the Annual Declaration of Compliance with the Bermuda Registrar and pay the Bermuda annual government fee (currently BMD 3,820–4,590 depending on share capital) to maintain the exempted status; maintain a non-resident exclusion certificate under the Bermuda Economic Substance Act by evidencing tax residence and management in Gibraltar.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — The Bermuda Exempted Company is exempt from Bermuda corporate income tax, capital gains tax, and withholding tax (0% headline, subject to the new 15% Bermuda Corporate Income Tax for MNE groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750 million effective fiscal year 2025, which does not apply to a boutique patent agency). In Gibraltar, the classification depends on the seat of management: if central management and control is exercised in Gibraltar, the company becomes a Gibraltar-resident company chargeable at 12.5% only on Gibraltar-source profits (territorial basis); income arising from patent prosecution work physically performed in Gibraltar is Gibraltar-source, while foreign-source income received outside Gibraltar remains outside the Gibraltar charge. The Exempted Company's structural prohibition on Bermuda local business is compatible, as all trading activity occurs through the Gibraltar operation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Gibraltar has no check-the-box election. Available statutory mechanisms include: (a) voluntary election for the Commissioner of Income Tax to treat a non-Gibraltar-incorporated company as tax resident in Gibraltar based on central management and control; (b) group relief election enabling transfer of losses between 75% Gibraltar-resident group companies (Income Tax Act 2010, s.65); (c) patent box (IP Box) election applying a preferential effective rate (historically 2.5%) to qualifying patent income derived from IP developed in Gibraltar; (d) capital allowance elections for qualifying IP assets; and (e) automatic application of OECD hybrid mismatch rules to neutralize double non-taxation arising from payments between the Bermuda exempted company and the Gibraltar taxable branch — no election to disapply is permitted. No election is available to opt out of the standard 12.5% corporation tax rate.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: No VAT or GST applies in Gibraltar. Gibraltar is constitutionally outside the UK VAT area and, post-Brexit, outside the EU VAT regime; indirect taxation is limited to customs and excise duties on imported physical goods, stamp duty on real estate transfers and instruments, and hydrocarbon duty. Supplies of PCT patent prosecution and international trademark registration services are entirely outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect tax. Bermuda similarly imposes no VAT or GST, but levies customs duties on imported goods (average ad valorem 15%–30% depending on classification) and a payroll tax on Bermuda-employed remuneration, which is not triggered by the Gibraltar operating entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Not applicable — no VAT/GST regime exists in Gibraltar, therefore no economic turnover threshold triggers indirect tax registration. Importers of dutiable physical goods must obtain a customs registration and account for duties via the Gibraltar Customs Department, but this does not apply to a service-only patent agency. In Bermuda, payroll tax registration is required only where Bermuda remuneration exceeds BMD 1,000 per month; the Exempted Company with zero Bermuda employees has no registration obligation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, tax-authority API integration, or digital stamping requirement exists in Gibraltar. Electronic invoices are accepted for statutory record-keeping and must be retained for at least six years, showing the Gibraltar TRN, the supplier's name and address, a sequential number, and the client's name and jurisdiction of residence. Physical goods declarations are processed electronically through the ASYCUDA World customs clearance system, but this applies to merchandise logistics only and not to professional or IP services.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Not applicable — because Gibraltar has no VAT/GST, cross-border supplies of patent prosecution and trademark registration services to clients in the USA, EU, WIPO, Singapore, and other foreign jurisdictions are simply outside the scope of Gibraltar indirect tax. No zero-rating claim, input VAT recovery mechanism, or refund procedure exists. Substantiation of the arm's-length and indirect-tax-free treatment requires the client engagement agreement, itemized fee schedules separating official filing fees (WIPO, USPTO, EPO, UKIPO) from agent professional fees, WIPO/PCT or Madrid System receipts, evidence of foreign payer status, and bank records showing cross-border inward remittance.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Not applicable to services — no customs export declaration is required for IP/patent prosecution supplies
Client engagement letter and power of attorney evidencing the patent/trademark agency mandate
Itemized invoices separating official filing fees (WIPO/USPTO/EPO/UKIPO) from agent professional fees
WIPO PCT or Madrid System receipt confirming international filing date and designated states
Inward remittance confirmation (SWIFT MT103) from the foreign client for each professional fee invoice
Gibraltar Tax Reference Number registration certificate and tax residence certificate
Bermuda Certificate of Exemption and annual Declaration of Compliance evidencing tax-exempt status
Transfer pricing documentation demonstrating arm's-length fees between the Bermuda entity and the Gibraltar operating presence
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: There is no statutory FX repatriation deadline in Gibraltar or Bermuda; the 180-day benchmark is applied as an administrative expectation consistent with OECD transfer pricing documentation standards and prudent treasury practice. Absent a VAT system, no export zero-rating clawback exists, but the following tax audit exposures apply: (a) Gibraltar Income Tax Act 2010 — a negligent or fraudulent tax return attracts civil penalties up to 100% of the tax understated plus interest at 8% per annum, with criminal liability on indictment (fine up to GBP 500,000 and/or imprisonment up to seven years); a discovery assessment may be raised within 21 years in cases of fraud or wilful default; (b) permanent establishment risk — if the Bermuda entity invoices for patent work performed in Gibraltar without a Gibraltar branch and arm's-length allocation, the Commissioner may deem a Gibraltar PE, reallocate 12.5% tax on Gibraltar-source profits, and impose penalties for failure to notify chargeability; (c) Gibraltar transfer pricing rules require contemporaneous documentation for cross-border related-party fee flows; non-compliance carries penalties of up to GBP 100,000; (d) mischaracterization of mark-ups on patent office fees as disimbursable at cost without substantiating WIPO receipts may be treated as undisclosed Gibraltar taxable turnover, giving rise to a 100% penalty plus interest; (e) Bermuda Economic Substance Act 2019 — if the entity cannot substantiate non-resident status, penalties start at USD 250,000 for the first year and USD 500,000 for each subsequent year, with possible strike-off; and (f) CRS/FATCA self-certification obligations apply to the professional services entity as a non-financial foreign entity, and incorrect filings attract Gibraltar penalties of up to GBP 50,000.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Government of Gibraltar - Financial Services Commission (banking supervisor and licensing authority) in coordination with HM Treasury, United Kingdom; Gibraltar has no autonomous central bank, and the Gibraltar pound (GIP) is issued by the Government of Gibraltar and pegged at 1:1 to GBP.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Gibraltar maintains full current-account convertibility and de facto full capital-account convertibility. There is no foreign-exchange control law, no Central Bank approval gate for inbound investment, and no restriction on profit repatriation or dividend distribution. GIP is freely exchangeable into GBP at par through authorised Gibraltar banks, and balances may be held in GBP, USD, EUR, or any major currency. For the custom 'Bermuda Exempted Co' structure, legal and beneficial owners may repatriate retained earnings by ordinary board resolution and bank wire, subject only to standard KYC and source-of-funds verification at the paying bank. No withholding or supplementary remittance tax is levied by Gibraltar on distributions to non-resident shareholders of an exempted company. Practical hurdles are limited to bank clearing times (CHAPS/Fedwire/SEPA) and correspondent-bank due diligence on the underlying patent-prosecution fee flow.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion applies to export receipts, including receipts from PCT patent prosecution, international trademark filing, or legal fee disbursements. Gibraltar does not impose an export-proceeds conversion ratio or obligatory holding period for foreign currency. The entity is free to retain all receipts in original currency, sell them to its bank on spot terms, or hedge them via permitted forward contracts. If receipts are in GIP, banks convert to GBP at par automatically at no net economic cost. The only administrative requirements are accounting substance records, transfer pricing documentation, and anti-money laundering transaction monitoring on high-frequency fee disbursements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Client Monies Escrow Account
Operational Account / Foreign Currency Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium for operational payment rails, Low for capital escrow and client-monies. Wise (natively suggested by the business model) and similar UK-authorized Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) may be used for low-value disbursements of filing fees, annuity payments, and vendor invoices in USD, EUR, and GBP. Legal constraints: EMIs are not deposit-taking banks, do not hold client money as a licensed bank, and cannot provide formal escrow accounts, dedicated account segregation for regulated legal-client funds, or direct clearing through CHAPS/Fedwire under payment-banking credentials. A cross-border digital EMI account may be onboarded remotely using passport and corporate registry, but the Gibraltar Financial Services Commission AML regime requires that client monies relating to patent prosecution remain in a bank-designated client account or in a licensed bank as principal. Therefore, the blueprint must use an EMI only as a funding/collection ancillary ledger, never as the custody rail for capital, settlement reserves, or lawyer-client trust moneys.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Gibraltar permits remote corporate account opening for low-risk professional services companies, subject to enhanced due diligence at the bank's discretion. Directors, ultimate beneficial owners, and signatories must submit notarized copies of passports and proof-of-address. A physical interview in Gibraltar is not statutorily mandatory for a legitimate patent-prosecution agency with a Bermuda Exempted Co wrapper; however, in practice most Tier-1 Gibraltar banks require at least one director or a nominated compliance officer to attend an in-person interview, either in Gibraltar or at a UK-based private-bank branch/reception office. Where any director, shareholder, or payment recipient is resident in a high-risk jurisdiction, the bank will require a physical interview at the Gibraltar head office or a video interview with live document verification plus an external professional introduction from a licensed Gibraltar or UK auditor/lawyer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or signatory is resident in a high-risk or FATF blacklisted jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled passport copies, recent utility bill or financial institution statement, Council of Europe/UK sanctions screening report, written source-of-funds explanation, tax residence certificate, and a professional reference from a UK/Gibraltar licensed accountant or attorney plus a notarized declaration of all beneficial ownership layers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bermuda Exempted Company ring-fencing, nominee officers, or statutory information opacity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, register of directors, register of members, beneficial ownership declaration, Bermuda registered agent comfort letter, confirmation that no bearer shares are outstanding, corporate-by-laws, resolutions approving the Gibraltar bank relationship, and a legal opinion from a Bermuda counsel confirming the entity is in good standing and not insolvent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing or unconvincing professional licence for patent prosecution services
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chartered Institute of Patent Attorneys (CIPA) or UK Intellectual Property Office registration, citizen or attorney membership, professional indemnity insurance certificate, regulatory status letter from the relevant IP office, client-vetting framework, terms of business, and a list of qualified patent agents/trademark attorneys who will supervise the work.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency fee wires to foreign patent offices without clear client identification
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed client engagement letters, fee-invoice breakdown with each patent/trademark application reference, WIPO/USPTO/EPO fee schedule mapping, board-approved disbursement policy, sworn undertaking that funds belong to disclosed clients, and a transaction monitoring mechanism that flags mismatches in beneficiary names or application numbers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptoasset capital injection or unverified source-of-wealth
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete source-of-wealth report prepared by a UK/Gibraltar ICAEW/ACCA accountant, verified exchange transaction history, public-blockchain wallet attribution report from a compliant analytics vendor, liquid-assets bank statement, tax compliance certificate, and a declaration that no funds originate from illicit IP infringement, ransomware, or sanctions evasion.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections shall be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the Bermuda parent account or shareholder account to a licensed Gibraltar bank account. For GBP, use CHAPS via the Gibraltar bank's UK settlement agent; for USD, use Fedwire or correspondent-bank internal book transfer; for EUR, use SEPA Instant or TARGET2. The wire must reference 'SHARE CAPITAL / SUBSCRIPTION' or 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' in field 70, accompanied by a board resolution approving the injection, a certified statement of the exempted-company no-par-value capital, and a Form from the corporate services provider confirming the capital is not loan proceeds. For the patent-prosecution agency model, recurring fee receipts from applicants are not capital injections; they should be marked as 'CLIENT FUNDS / FILING FEES' and, if aggregated, must be held in a segregated client account. Where a Wise payout is used for a client's refund, the money trail must reconcile exactly from the receiving bank, through the client ledger, to the designated applicant wallet.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail for official patent-office payments is SWIFT MT103 to WIPO, USPTO, EPO, UKIPO, and national IP-office beneficiaries; each wire includes the official application or international registration number in instruction fields. Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) are not the standard clearing rail for patent prosecution fees and are generally limited to high-value annuities or bulk litigation settlements, advised through a Gibraltar confirming bank. Secondary rails include: SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for EUIPO and EPO, US domestic ACH or Fedwire for USPTO direct-pay, and Wise for minor renewal fees in low-value currencies, subject to the licensee maintaining audit reconciliation between the client file and the Wise transaction ID. Disbursements must never be made to non-state third parties without a signed invoice and written client instruction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: GBP/USD outright FX forward (non-deliverable not required as GBP/USD is fully convertible)
GIP/GBP free-swap no hedge required due to exchange-rate parity
CHF/USD forward for WIPO fee exposure

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on restricted currencies (e.g., RUB, CNY, INR) only when the corresponding patent-office disbursement or client payment is denominated in that currency and local conversion is administratively unavailable; must be evidenced by an underlying patent fee invoice
Cross-currency swap (USD/EUR or GBP/USD) approved by the board on a non-speculative basis for matching the entity's multi-year competitor annuity or litigation fee commitments

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 12.5% flat rate on Gibraltar-resident companies' worldwide trading income, and on non-resident companies' income attributable to a Gibraltar permanent establishment (Income Tax Act 2010, as amended); the Bermuda Exempted Company enjoys no Bermuda-imposed income tax under its exemption certificate (valid through 2035), but that Bermuda exemption does not override Gibraltar corporate tax on profits managed and controlled from Gibraltar.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Gibraltar Patent Box reduces the effective rate to 10% on qualifying patented-technology exploitation profits (12.5% statutory rate reduced by the 20% Patent Box deduction, subject to modified-nexus and substance requirements); ordinary PCT agency fees remain trading income taxed at 12.5%; capital allowances available on office/computer infrastructure; inter-company dividend participation exemption prevents double taxation on qualifying distributions. The old Qualifying Overseas Subsidiary (QOS) exemption regime is inapplicable prospectively following EU state-aid determinations.
